That is why `git switch` executed while ui-control.js orchestratorGate had denied it since c7ab206 — the gate was never in the loop. FIX APPLIED: plugin/hooks/block-main-loop-mutations.sh — role gate (agent_id absent = main loop), mutating git DENY, merge/promote (gh pr merge, issuekit pr merge / promote / branch prune --apply) ASK, read-only git + the rest of issuekit + all sub-agents untouched, add/commit carved out to the pack's commit-gate when installed. 26 branches exercised, all pass. REMAINING: our hooks only reach a session that LOADS this plugin (web UI automatically; terminal via `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install`). The observed environment ships hooks we do not, so confirm the plugin is actually installed there — if it is not, this fix does not reach it and the gap is an INSTALL gap, not a code gap. Original row text below. UNEXPLAINED BYPASS — needs a repro before any fix. The main-loop mutating-git deny DOES exist and DOES cover `switch`: ui/server/core/ui-control.js orchestratorGate() denies Bash for agent === 'main' when GIT_MUTATE_RE matches, wired through session-permissions.js:65 preToolGate, landed c7ab206 (2026-08-01, 'mutating git denied for the main loop'). Yet the 2026-08-17 post-mortem that filed the now-deleted D8-spine-claims-git-deny-that-does-not-exist observed an orchestrator running `git switch` a dozen times in one session. Both cannot be true of the same session. Two candidate explanations, UNTESTED: (a) that session was a plain Claude Code CLI session on the bound project, not a UI-server session — the gate lives in canUseTool, which only exists in the server's SDK session, and ui/orchestrator-spine.md is likewise only loaded by config.js buildSystemPrompt, so a CLI session gets NEITHER the sentence nor the gate and the claim is simply out of scope there; (b) the gate ran and did not fire (agent field not 'main' for the main loop under some path, or the command shape dodged the regex — e.g. an `rtk`-prefixed form, a heredoc, or git invoked via a wrapper). RESOLVE BY EVIDENCE, not by adding a second layer: find the post-mortem's session log, check whether it was a server session, and grep the permission log for policy:'orchestrator-gate' entries around those git calls. If (a), the real gap is that CORE ships no main-loop git guard for CLI-bound sessions and the hook layer (plugin/hooks/block-destructive-git.sh, which is role-blind by design) is the only thing present there — decide then whether that is a gap worth a hook or an accepted scope boundary. If (b), it is a live gate defect and takes priority. Filed 2026-08-17 while applying the deleted row, whose premise ('no such deny exists') was FALSE — it audited plugin/hooks/ only and missed the permission layer.

Countable next audit: sessions with dispatches and no open objective; dispatches after the objective closed. STILL OPEN — the CLOSURE half: nothing measures generated-vs-closed. Pulse HAS been running (owner, 2026-09-04) — measure from real beats before designing the note-class check. | ORIGINAL: Nothing carries the human's OBJECTIVE across turns, so each turn re-derives its goal from the freshest thing in context. Observed live: 'close these issues' drifted to fix deploy -> fix gate -> fix red main -> reconcile branches, ending with 3 new PRs + 1 framework issue while open issues moved 24 -> 20. NOT a missing rule: ui/orchestrator-spine.md:73-74 already says 'Never silently expand scope … a change broader than the agreed slice → stop' and :15 says 'cut ONE small slice' — the prohibition exists and was violated, so restating it harder is the label-for-a-label move (cf. D8-qa-pass-not-bound-to-sha). The MECHANISM gap is precise: the only thing in the framework that holds an objective is Autonomous Mode (standing Main Goal in .xenomoon/autonomous.json, with check turns that RESTATE the goal every tick — autonomous-main-goal/SKILL.md:9), and it is heavyweight (must be armed, self-drives, and escalates permissions via session.autonomousActive). For a plain ask there is no lightweight equivalent. Precedent for the shape of a fix already exists in the spine: it has restate-discipline for EXECUTION SHAPE ('after a correction, restate the shape in one line before dispatching anything else') but nothing for OBJECTIVE. SECOND HALF: nothing anywhere measures CLOSURE — every loop we ship counts production (tasks created, promotions filed, findings logged, epics charted), so the generated-vs-closed ratio is invisible to every mechanism in the repo, and what is not measured does not get optimised. The fix is NOT another rule and NOT a fourth subsystem beside Autonomous/epics/Pulse — reaching for a new mechanism here would enact the very failure. Design first, like Pulse got. Candidate for the closure half only: a note-class Pulse check (see D9-pulse-amplifies-scope-drift) firing on a worsening ratio, since that is deterministic state over time and fits machinery that already exists.
  - _pattern:_ an objective the human stated is durable and restated before each dispatch — a prohibition against drifting is not a mechanism for holding the aim.
